title: Basin reserve-web fragment viability
scope: Threshold-based survival and possible independent-patch stabilization of severed reserve-web fragments in Project Hearthway's initial basin. Exact quantitative thresholds, anatomy, wound response, timescale, reconnection, other reproduction, species variation, Mana use, System appraisal, and human knowledge or exploitation remain open.
approval_evidence: After the threshold-based fragment-survival recommendation was presented, the Author replied 'yes' on 2026-08-14.
question: Under what general condition can a severed reserve-web section survive and become an independent colony patch?
selection: Severed fragments survive only when they retain enough viable modules, reserves, and functioning connections to sustain themselves. Viable fragments can slowly stabilize as independent patches; inadequate fragments decline and die. Fragmentation therefore does not make every break an effortless propagation event.
alternatives: FLORA-FRAGMENT-A: threshold-based viability followed by possible slow independent-patch stabilization; selected.
FLORA-FRAGMENT-B: universal or near-universal survival of living fragments; not selected.
FLORA-FRAGMENT-C: isolated fragments cannot become independent patches; not selected.
rationale: The selected rule preserves the reserve-web's capacity for local recovery while making fragmentation conditional, slow, materially constrained, and capable of failure rather than an automatic propagation or refill mechanism.
consequences: Severance creates only a candidate fragment rather than a guaranteed new patch.
Independent survival requires enough viable modules, reserves, and functioning connections for self-maintenance.
A viable fragment can slowly stabilize as an independent patch.
An inadequate fragment cannot persist independently and declines and dies.
Exact thresholds, timescale, wound response, reconnection, and other reproductive routes remain open.
Independent patch status does not establish a personal System actor, duplicated identity, spawn, refill, or progression reward.
residual_unknowns: Minimum functional module count, reserve condition, connection topology, and interactions among those requirements remain open.
Stabilization timescale, mortality curve, wound response, and seasonal variation remain open.
Reconnection, fusion, competition, parasitism, and disease transmission remain open.
Biological individuality, genetic relationship, displaced-fragment survival, and other reproduction or dispersal routes remain open.
Mana use, System appraisal, human knowledge, and deliberate propagation remain open.
reopening_conditions: Detailed ecological modelling cannot support viable fragments without automatic propagation.
Later species design requires a materially different fragment-survival rule.
A story requirement exposes an unresolvable contradiction in damage, recovery, reproduction, or identity.
The Author explicitly reopens the decision.
